ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-25), cover page, securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b): 'Ordinary shares, par value EUR 0.01 per share', trading symbol FER, 'Nasdaq Global Select Market' — the Nasdaq security is the ordinary share itself, not an ADS

This is not an unanchored estimate — it is the filer's own cash-flow statement figure for FY2025 (see source), and no engine-readable filed capex value exists in any period to anchor to.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads (no ifrs-full PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipment concept exists in this filer's companyfacts at all). The engine applies this single FY2025 filing value to every missing period; for FY2023 it overstates true capex (EUR 86M filed) in the conservative direction, for FY2024 it understates it by EUR 39M (EUR 226M filed) — immaterial against OCF of EUR 1,263M-1,926M in those years. Declared in EUR (the reporting currency); the engine FX-converts at period-end ECB rates. Infrastructure-project investments (a separate cash-flow line, EUR 466M in FY2025) are concession growth investments, not PP&E/intangible capex, and are not in this line — see analysis.md.
capex_override.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-25), Consolidated statements of cash flows, investing activities line 'Investments in property, plant and equipment/intangible assets' (Note 3.4): EUR 187M for FY2025, with EUR 226M for FY2024 and EUR 86M for FY2023 in the same statement (tagged in the filing's inline XBRL under the custom fer:InvestmentsInPropertyPlantAndEquipmentAndIntangibleAssets concept, which EDGAR companyfacts does not carry)

moat_justification: The highways portfolio is genuinely scarce: a 48.29% stake in Toronto's 407 ETR and majority stakes in US congestion-priced managed lanes (NTE, LBJ, NTE 35W, I-77, I-66) sit in corridors that cannot be replicated, with dynamic/inflation-linked toll pricing power proven over cycles (H1 2026 revenue per transaction +8.7% to +18.9% across the US lanes; 407 ETR approved a further CAD 550M dividend for Q3 2026). Airports add scarce gateway capacity (49% of JFK New Terminal One, 60% of Dalaman). Against that: the crown jewels are minority/JV stakes Ferrovial does not fully control, toll-setting is politically exposed, concessions are finite-lived, and most consolidated revenue is construction — a competitive-bid business running at a ~3.5% adjusted EBIT margin with no pricing power. Net: moderate moat, 6/10, carried by the toll-road concessions and diluted by construction and non-control.
moat_for: 407 ETR (48.29% stake): irreplaceable Toronto corridor under a long concession, proven toll pricing power and large recurring dividends
US managed lanes (NTE, LBJ, NTE 35W, I-77, I-66): congestion-based dynamic tolling in corridors that cannot be duplicated; H1 2026 revenue/transaction grew +8.7% to +18.9%, well above inflation
Inflation-linked concession cash flows with decades-long remaining lives and extreme permitting/replication barriers
Scarce airport capacity positions: 49% of JFK New Terminal One and 60% of Dalaman Airport
Record EUR 18B construction order book (North America 47.9%) gives forward revenue visibility
moat_against: Crown jewels are minority/JV stakes (407 ETR 48.29%, JFK NTO 49%) — dividend and strategy decisions are shared, not controlled
Political/regulatory exposure on tolls (Ontario pressure on 407 ETR pricing; US managed-lane backlash) and finite concession lives
Most consolidated revenue is construction: competitive bidding, ~3.5% adjusted EBIT margin target, no pricing power
Capital-intensive concession model: value arrives as equity-accounted dividends, and consolidated net debt was EUR 6,283M at H1 2026 (mostly non-recourse project debt)
Reported profit is flattered by asset-rotation gains (a EUR 2,208M disposal-gain line in FY2024 net income), so headline earnings overstate recurring economics
one_liner: High-quality toll-road concessions (moat 6/10) inside a mostly-construction consolidator — at $50.34 the weighted IRR is only 9.5% (IV@15% $25.63), so it does not clear the 15% hurdle; it would need a price at or below ~$25.63 to clear 15% on these numbers.
